follow_ups.title: Add socket_connect_timeout to conftest redis_client
follow_ups.description: The current conftest.py uses redis.Redis.from_url(...) with default settings. On a host where Redis is unreachable, the client.ping() in the fixture hangs indefinitely (default socket_connect_timeout=None). For local-dev UX, add socket_connect_timeout=1 so a missing Redis fails fast with a ConnectionError. Trivial one-line fix; not blocking the merge because CI provides Redis via the services: block.

notes: Phase C step 2 completes issue #5 AC-2.4 — Sessions stored in Redis 7 with 8h idle / 30d max TTL. The 38-test TTL contract from Phase C step 1 (PR #49) is now satisfied by two backends: InMemorySessionManager and RedisSessionManager, both implementations of the SessionManager ABC.

The Redis backend ships with implementation-level confidence but no live CI signal. This is a deliberate conductor decision (merge without the workflow commit) and is captured in follow-up-1. The orchestrator's recommendation in the PR body was to paste the workflow commit first; the conductor chose the alternative path. The implementation itself is sound — code review confirmed correct Lua atomicity, clock injection as source of truth, post-script audit emission, and the EXPIREAT guard against past-time. The risk is that a future regression in the Redis backend would not be caught by CI until follow-up-1 is complete.

The InMemorySessionManager remains the primary contract surface (the 38 tests are written against its fixture signature). The RedisSessionManager is a drop-in replacement at the SessionManager ABC boundary. If the implementation is later extracted to a config-driven factory pattern (per Phase D roadmap), no further contract work is needed.

Production deployment of RedisSessionManager (vs InMemorySessionManager) is a separate AC: issue #4 AC-1.4 covers provisioning + REDIS_URL injection via the deployment platform. That work is gated on Phase 2 of the rollout plan documented in REDIS_BACKEND_DESIGN.md §13.
